title: Cooking Food
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Deep frying in class is a teacher demonstration only, children standing a metre back. Children may dry fat fry minced meat or bacon-like fatty meat under close watch.

skills.key_step: The child describes dry fat frying (cooking fatty food in its own fat in a pan with little or no oil added: minced meat, sausages, fatty meat) and deep frying (food covered in hot oil: chips, mandazi, samosas, fish) and the foods that suit each.

floor.question: How much oil is used in shallow frying?

representations: pictures of a dry pan with sausages and a deep pan of oil
steps: Dry fat frying: the food's own fat, little or no oil.
Deep frying: food covered in hot oil.
Match the food to the method.

board.do: Draw a deep pot with mandazi floating in oil.

misconceptions.ask: How much oil does deep frying use?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a pan of mandazi frying in deep oil and eggs frying in a little oil.

misconceptions.ask: Sausages are cooked in a pan with no added oil. Which method is this?
misconceptions.repair: Warm sausages in a dry pan and watch the fat come out.

misconceptions.ask: Which food is usually deep fried?
misconceptions.repair: Ask whether the food floats in oil or cooks in its own fat.

misconceptions.ask: When is food put into the oil for deep frying?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a piece fried from cold oil (greasy) with one put into hot oil (crisp).

checks.question: Which method is used for mandazi?
Why is little or no oil added in dry fat frying?
checks.answer: the food cooks in its own fat

skills.key_step: The child says how to fry safely (dry the food, fill the pan only a third, lower food in gently away from you, never leave hot oil, a lid or damp cloth for an oil fire, never water) and how to serve fried food (drain on paper, serve hot, clean up).

floor.question: Which method covers food in oil?

representations: a pan marked at one third
a lid and a dry cloth
steps: Fill the pan only a third.
Stay with the pan; lid for a fire.

board.do: Draw a pan of oil with flames.
Wait for "cover it with a lid or damp cloth, turn off the heat".
Write "never water on an oil fire".

misconceptions.ask: A pan of oil catches fire. What do you do?
misconceptions.repair: Show with a teacher why water and hot oil spit and spread the fire.

listen_for: Water in the oil makes no difference
misconceptions.ask: Why should food be dry before it goes into hot oil?
misconceptions.repair: Dry one piece and leave another wet, drop each into a safe test with a teacher.

misconceptions.ask: How full should the pan be for deep frying?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what happens when food goes into a full pan.

listen_for: Go and answer, the oil will wait
misconceptions.ask: Hot oil is on the stove and the phone rings. What do you do?
misconceptions.repair: Ask how fast oil heats and when it smokes.

checks.question: Why is wet food dangerous in hot oil?
checks.answer: the water spits and the oil can burn you

checks.question: How full should a deep-frying pan be?
